records.question: Summarize all the rules in the fraud memo.
records.answer: The fraud rules memo effective March 1, 2026, sets real-time card fraud thresholds [1][2]. The rules include R-101 Velocity, which declines the sixth and later card-not-present purchases and texts the customer when there are six or more within 10 minutes [6]. R-104 Geo-jump declines the second purchase and places a soft block for two card-present purchases more than 500 miles apart within 2 hours [6]. R-110 First foreign use triggers in-app step-up verification for a first-ever foreign purchase over $400 [6]. R-117 Merchant risk holds transactions for analyst review for up to 4 hours when the merchant category is high-risk and the amount is over $250 [6]. R-122 New-device spend declines purchases over $1,000 within 24 hours of a new device enrolling and requires a call to Customer Care [6]. R-130 ATM pattern blocks ATM access for 24 hours following 3 or more out-of-network ATM withdrawals in one day at different terminals [6].

records.question: What did Microsoft list as its main risks in its latest annual report?
records.answer: In its fiscal year 2025 annual report, Microsoft listed several risks and uncertainties, including intense competition across all markets for its products and services [1], global, regional, and local economic developments and trade policy changes such as tariffs and import or export controls [3], and risks related to advertising, professional, marketplace, and gaming platform abuses [2]. Additional risks included other digital safety abuses, geopolitical tensions, sanctions, climate change, and risks relating to the evolution of its business such as business model competition and the use of AI systems [4][5][6].
